title: The Wise Men of Chelm and the Fence Against the Cold
summary: It's freezing in Chelm, and Reb Zalman has a brilliant idea: put an iron-wire fence around the whole town so the cold gets stuck outside! All of Chelm builds it, and in the morning Reb Kalman reaches past the fence: "Oy, how cold it is out there!" But little Gitele knows how people really get warm. A rhyming story based on a folk tale of the Wise Men of Chelm.
pages:
In Chelm it was freezing, the wind whistled through,
red noses, blue fingers, and nobody felt good, it's true.
"A stove warms for an hour," sighed Yokel, "then we freeze once again!
Who will find us an answer? Nu, where are the wise men?"

Tall Reb Zalman stood on a stool and declared, very grand:
"The cold comes from outside! We'll stop it — no regrets, understand!
We'll wrap Chelm in iron wire, all the way round, on every side,
and the cold won't get in — it will just have to stay outside!"

Everyone clapped: "How clever! What an idea! What a plan!"
And old Reb Shmerel scratched his beard: "Hmm... what a genius man!"

The four strong men dragged rolls of iron, long and heavy to tow,
and Yokel ran after them with a hammer, shouting, "Hooray, friends, let's go!"
The children carried the pegs, and the old folks held the wire tight,
and all Chelm worked together, with singing and laughing and smiles so bright.

They hammered a peg, stretched a wire, round every house and every yard,
till the circle was closed, with no holes and no gaps, not a single crack unbarred.
A fence round the town — oh, what perfect order!
The cold stays outside — it can't cross the border!

Everyone went home with big, wide smiles and delight,
breathed in deep and said, "Now we can sleep without worry tonight!"
A fence round the town — oh, what perfect order!
The cold stays outside — it can't cross the border!

In the morning Reb Kalman went out and reached his hand past the fence,
and suddenly: "Oy, oy! How cold it is out there! That's not right, it makes no sense!"
Then all Chelm came to the fence and stuck their hands outside —
"How cold it is out there!" they all shouted. "The fence works! What a success!" they cried.

Chatter-chatter-chatter went teeth all over Chelm, in every yard,
but nobody noticed — they were all staring at the fence so hard.
A fence round the town — oh, what perfect order!
The cold stays outside — it can't cross the border!

Little Gitele raised a finger: "But it's cold in here too, inside!"
Reb Zalman said, "That's a different cold! An inside cold — it never crossed from outside!"

Gitele brought a big pot of soup, all steaming and hot,
and gave everyone a bowl: "This one's for you, and for you, and for..." — the whole lot!
They sat snug together and laughed, as the bowls sent up steam to the sky,
and their noses turned pink, and their ears got warm — oh my!

That night the snow fell, and the fence sparkled silver and bright,
and the people of Chelm slept soundly, blankets up to their noses, all night.
In the morning Reb Kalman reached his hand out over the border:
"Oy, how cold it is out there!" — and everyone: "What perfect order!"
